lessons.title: Recognize an emergency and activate an effective response
lessons.body:
Begin with scene safety: traffic, electricity, hazardous atmosphere and moving equipment can injure the rescuer. Do not enter a toxic atmosphere or contact an energized casualty. Once access is safe, check responsiveness and normal breathing, obtain consent when the person can respond, and activate emergency services for a life-threatening condition. An unresponsive adult with absent or abnormal breathing, including gasping, may be in cardiac arrest. Lay rescuers should not delay action with an unreliable pulse search. Put a mobile call on speaker when feasible and follow dispatcher coaching. Assign a specific person to bring the AED and another to meet responders at the access point; vague requests to a crowd often go unfulfilled. Protect yourself from blood and bodily fluids using available barriers without unnecessarily delaying lifesaving care.

Worked case
A contractor collapses next to a parked truck. The scene is safe, the contractor is unresponsive and only gasps occasionally. Those gasps are not reassuring normal breathing. A colleague calls emergency services on speaker and identifies the gate, another retrieves the AED, and a rescuer begins appropriate CPR. If the same collapse occurred inside an alarmed vessel, the initial action would be emergency activation and specialist rescue, not entry by the first aider.

Application and instructor observation
The instructor presents safe and unsafe scene cards. The learner must distinguish an accessible collapse from a hazardous rescue, identify abnormal breathing and allocate response tasks by name. Record time lost to unnecessary debate, missing location information and failure to request the AED. Use only a manikin for physical rehearsal and follow the current recognized curriculum.

lessons.title: Adult CPR: quality, feedback and fatigue
lessons.body:
For adult cardiac arrest, high-quality chest compressions create blood flow while definitive help is coming. Current AHA guidance uses a rate of 100–120 compressions per minute and depth of at least 2 inches (5 cm), avoiding excessive depth above 2.4 inches (6 cm) in an average adult. Allow full recoil and minimize interruptions. A trained rescuer who can provide breaths follows the current adult 30-compressions-to-2-breaths sequence; an untrained or unwilling bystander can provide compression-only CPR for a sudden adult collapse with dispatcher assistance. This adult lesson does not transfer automatically to drowning, pediatric or professional-rescuer algorithms. Quality is a combination, not merely speed: shallow rapid compressions or leaning on the chest can be ineffective. Feedback manikins help learners identify these errors. Rescuers should coordinate changes to limit fatigue and pauses.

Worked case
On a manikin a learner performs 150 shallow compressions in a minute and claims that more is better. The instructor shows the rate is above the recommended range and depth is inadequate. The next trial targets 110 per minute with measured depth and full recoil. In another trial the learner reaches correct depth but pauses repeatedly to discuss performance; minimizing those interruptions becomes the specific coaching goal.

Application and instructor observation
Use a feedback manikin and the provider skill sheet. Observe hand position, measured rate and depth, recoil, interruptions and response to fatigue. Do not mark the skill passed from a verbal answer or a stopwatch count alone. The learner must repeat the performance successfully after feedback. Practice breaths with the appropriate barrier and equipment under the instructor curriculum.

lessons.title: AED use and coordinated resuscitation
lessons.body:
An AED analyzes heart rhythm and advises whether a shock is appropriate. It does not replace CPR or emergency activation. Turn it on, expose and prepare the chest as directed, and place pads according to the device diagrams. Follow its voice prompts. Everyone must be clear during rhythm analysis and shock delivery; touching the casualty can interfere with analysis and create shock exposure. After a shock, or when no shock is advised, resume CPR promptly as directed rather than assuming the emergency has ended. A no-shock message is a rhythm decision, not proof that circulation has returned. Device readiness matters before an emergency: accessible storage, visible signage, working status indication and in-date supplies help prevent avoidable delay. Follow device instructions for special circumstances and do not improvise pad placement or modify equipment.

Worked case
Two rescuers are performing CPR when the trainer AED arrives. One operates the device while the other maintains compressions until analysis is required. The operator gives a clear verbal warning and visually checks that nobody is touching the manikin. The device advises no shock; the team immediately resumes CPR. A trainee who walks away because the device did not shock has confused treatment selection with recovery.

Application and instructor observation
Use a trainer AED, never a live shock on a person for training. The evaluator observes pad placement, clear checks, prompt-following, coordination and rapid resumption of compressions. Introduce a no-shock scenario and an unavailable-supply scenario. Require the learner to explain both the immediate response and the readiness correction that prevents the same delay later.

lessons.title: Severe bleeding, shock and injury assessment
lessons.body:
Life-threatening bleeding needs rapid emergency activation and immediate control within training. Use a barrier and firm direct pressure at the bleeding site. For severe extremity bleeding, a trained provider may use a manufactured tourniquet according to the recognized curriculum and device instructions; improvised technique and casual removal can be dangerous. Record the application time for responders. Shock is inadequate circulation to tissues; pale or clammy skin, weakness, altered responsiveness and rapid breathing are concerning findings. Control the cause when possible, keep the casualty protected from temperature extremes and monitor breathing. Do not provide food or drink to a seriously injured person. Avoid unnecessary movement when major trauma is suspected, except when needed for immediate safety or lifesaving care. A first aider describes findings and changes rather than diagnosing internal injuries from appearance alone.

Worked case
A sharp edge causes heavy arm bleeding. The first aider uses gloves and direct pressure while another person calls for help. Bleeding remains severe and the trained responder applies the available approved tourniquet using the taught procedure, then records time. A coworker suggests loosening it every few minutes; the responder does not adopt that improvisation and hands management to emergency clinicians. The written exercise assesses recognition and priorities, not tourniquet skill.

Application and instructor observation
Use a bleeding-control trainer and the current provider lesson. Evaluate hazard recognition, barrier use, emergency activation, effective pressure, appropriate escalation and accurate handover. For tourniquet assessment use a training device and instructor-approved simulator, never tighten a device on an unsuspecting person. A learner must distinguish persistent life-threatening bleeding from a minor injury and explain the monitoring plan.

lessons.title: Burns, sudden illness and exposure-aware care
lessons.body:
Different causes require different scene controls. Electrical injury requires confirmation that the electrical hazard is controlled before contact. Chemical exposure requires avoiding contamination and following the substance-specific emergency information and dispatcher or medical guidance; an eyewash or shower must be reachable before work begins. For thermal burns, stop the burning process safely and use the current recognized first-aid cooling and covering instructions; do not apply grease or break blisters. Serious burns need professional assessment. Sudden chest discomfort, stroke signs, severe breathing difficulty or altered consciousness require rapid emergency activation. For suspected stroke, note when the person was last known well; that information can affect treatment. With seizures, protect from surrounding hazards, do not restrain the person and do not put objects in the mouth. Monitor breathing and follow emergency guidance.

Worked case
A worker suddenly has facial asymmetry and difficulty speaking. The first aider calls emergency services and learns from a witness that speech was normal at 09:10. Recording last-known-well at 09:10 is more useful than guessing that symptoms began when discovered at 09:25. In a separate splash scenario, approaching without chemical protection could contaminate the responder; the team activates the exposure plan and communicates the product information.

Application and instructor observation
The instructor uses illness and exposure cards. Ask the learner to identify the urgent finding, the information that changes care and the first avoidable mistake. Evaluate correct last-known-well reporting, safe handling of seizure scenarios and recognition of electrical or chemical rescue hazards. Do not practice medication administration or exposure treatment on people as part of this written course.

lessons.title: Team drills, clinical handover and qualification route
lessons.body:
A concise handover gives the event, observed condition, important times, care provided and changes. Use plain observations such as unresponsive and gasping, not a speculative diagnosis. Include AED shocks or no-shock prompts, CPR start and bleeding-control details when known. Protect private health information from unnecessary distribution. After the event, replenish supplies, report exposure through the employer process and offer support to responders. Readiness is a system: a trained person without accessible equipment or a remote team without a reliable call route may still be unable to respond effectively. Drill the actual call, gate and location interfaces without making a false emergency dispatch. A skills certificate comes from a recognized provider after its required instruction and observed assessment. An employer separately decides staffing, coverage and site responsibilities.

Worked case
A site has two trained first aiders, but both are assigned to a remote area while the workshop is occupied. The coverage plan is incomplete despite two current certificates. A tabletop drill also finds the ambulance gate locked after hours. Corrective actions redistribute coverage and establish a tested access arrangement. The next drill measures whether location and access information reach the responder, not merely whether a meeting occurred.

Application and instructor observation
Run an adult-collapse simulation with a manikin, trainer AED, simulated dispatcher and responder handoff. Score scene safety, recognition, activation, CPR/AED performance against the provider sheet, communication and transition to incoming care. Any unsafe entry or shock-clearance failure requires correction and reassessment. Keep the provider skills record separate from the VNDRLY knowledge record and employer coverage decision.

explanations.OG20_specialist_4_check2: MT relies on magnetic flux leakage in a suitably magnetized ferromagnetic material.
explanations.OG20_specialist_4_check3: The evidence must identify the actual inspected weld; plausible similarity cannot establish traceability.
explanations.OG20_specialist_5_check1: A new pressure-boundary feature may alter stresses and design requirements; classification precedes execution.
explanations.OG20_specialist_5_check3: Approval and performance are separate states requiring separate evidence.
explanations.OG20_specialist_6_check1: Exam references are window-specific and can differ from the newest published standard.
explanations.OG20_specialist_6_check2: The calculation addresses a specific thickness margin and assumed rate, not a changed design envelope.
explanations.OG20_specialist_6_check3: Tables must be applied with their notes, exceptions and scope.

lessons.title: Vessel inspection planning and damage hypotheses
lessons.body:
A vessel inspection starts with a defensible equipment boundary. Reconcile the nameplate, manufacturer data report, drawings, material records and modification history. Record design pressure and temperature, minimum design metal temperature where established, weld configuration, heat treatment, corrosion allowance and relief-system interfaces. Separate known values from assumptions. Operating pressure is not a substitute for a documented allowable pressure.

Build a damage hypothesis from material, process chemistry, temperature, stress and time. Wet carbon-steel service may involve general thinning, localized attack or wet-H2S damage; cyclic thermal service introduces a different concern. Examine startup, shutdown and upset history as well as normal operation. Map each credible mechanism to susceptible locations: liquid interfaces, nozzles, injection zones, supports, insulation terminations and welded attachments. A convenient thickness grid can miss a narrow damage zone.

For a separator with water accumulating at the bottom, specify examination of the lower shell and interfaces rather than extrapolating upper-shell readings. If external insulation is damaged near a support, include external corrosion investigation even when internal process corrosion is low. Visual inspection, thickness measurement and crack-sensitive examination answer different questions and should be combined deliberately.

Workshop evidence: produce a marked drawing, mechanism-location table and inspection plan stating method, access, coverage, preparation and limitations. An assessor checks whether each proposed method could detect the hypothesized morphology and whether inaccessible regions remain explicit. Reject a plan that declares inaccessible metal satisfactory or uses entry permission as proof of equipment integrity. This is a planning assessment; actual vessel entry requires the separately established isolation, atmosphere and rescue controls.

lessons.title: Corrosion rates, remaining life and measurement uncertainty
lessons.body:
A corrosion rate is a thickness change divided by elapsed time at a comparable location. Keep units visible. A historical reading of 12.0 mm and a current reading of 10.8 mm six years later give a long-term rate of (12.0−10.8)/6 = 0.20 mm/year. If the reading two years ago was 11.4 mm, the short-term rate is (11.4−10.8)/2 = 0.30 mm/year. Investigate the difference rather than automatically selecting the more favorable result. Process change, measurement positioning or accelerated attack may explain it.

For an educational case with an engineering-established required thickness of 8.4 mm, remaining life using 0.30 mm/year is (10.8−8.4)/0.30 = 8 years. This calculation is an extrapolation, not an inspection interval. Applicable code limits, mechanism behavior, reliability of measurements and risk decisions constrain the actual interval. Cracking cannot be managed by assuming the uniform-thinning equation describes its growth.

Thickness records must preserve location, technique, surface condition, temperature correction where applicable, instrument identity and reference checks. A 0.1 mm apparent change with readings each uncertain by ±0.2 mm does not establish a reliable small corrosion rate. Negative apparent corrosion may reflect measurement scatter or deposition; it does not prove that metal has regenerated.

Exercise: compute both rates, explain why the recent rate deserves attention, and propose confirmatory measurements at the same mapped locations. The assessor requires correct arithmetic and a recommendation that separates calculated life from permitted service. A passing worksheet includes assumptions and units and does not extrapolate an average across a local thin area.

lessons.title: Pressure, stress and wall calculations
lessons.body:
Pressure creates membrane stresses in a cylindrical shell. In a thin-wall educational model, circumferential stress is approximately PD/(2t), where pressure P and stress use consistent units, diameter D and wall thickness t use the same length unit, and end effects and local stress concentrations are excluded. Longitudinal membrane stress is approximately PD/(4t). The hoop stress is therefore about twice the longitudinal value for this simplified geometry.

At P = 1 MPa, D = 1000 mm and t = 10 mm, hoop stress is approximately 50 MPa. Reducing wall thickness to 8 mm increases it to 62.5 MPa at the same pressure. These relationships explain why wall loss matters; they are not the API/ASME acceptance equations. Actual calculations depend on the applicable shell/head equation, radius convention, weld joint efficiency, material allowable stress, temperature, corrosion allowance, static head and other loads.

For another educational model, t = PR/(SE−0.6P), with supplied values P = 1 MPa, R = 500 mm, S = 100 MPa and E = 1, yields 500/99.4 = 5.03 mm before any separately required allowances. The equation is supplied for arithmetic practice, not asserted applicable to every vessel. Reducing E to 0.85 raises this model result to 5.92 mm. Never assume joint efficiency from appearance.

The calculation assessment requires identifying the supplied equation's validity conditions, checking units, calculating independently and listing omitted loads. External-pressure buckling, heads, nozzles and local thin areas need their own rules. A competent submission explicitly refuses to turn this simplified result into an unrestricted maximum allowable working pressure.

lessons.title: Welding, heat treatment and examination strategy
lessons.body:
A repair weld joins materials while changing their thermal history. The welding procedure specification gives production instructions; the procedure qualification record records the test variables and results supporting a qualified procedure where required; the welder performance record establishes the individual's qualified range. A qualified welder does not make an unsupported procedure acceptable, and an acceptable procedure does not qualify every welder.

Review base-metal identification, thickness, filler selection, joint preparation, preheat/interpass controls, heat input where controlled, postweld heat treatment and examination requirements before fabrication. Hydrogen-assisted cracking needs attention to susceptible microstructure, hydrogen and tensile stress. Moisture control and preheat may reduce risk under an approved procedure, but arbitrary heating is not a substitute for metallurgical review.

Match examination to likely flaws. Visual inspection finds accessible surface conditions and dimensional deviations. PT targets surface-breaking flaws on suitable nonporous surfaces. MT requires ferromagnetic material. UT and RT have different orientation, geometry and access limitations. A rounded volumetric indication and a planar lack-of-fusion indication need different interpretation even if their apparent lengths match.

A repair pack exercise supplies a carbon-steel vessel, WPS revision B, a welder record for a different process and an NDE report referring to weld 14 instead of weld 41. The learner must identify both qualification and traceability failures before accepting the pack. The assessor retains the comparison table and marked weld map. Critical errors include substituting a procedure without approval, inferring acceptance from a smooth surface, or silently changing the NDE weld identifier. Required acceptance clauses and examination extent must come from the actual adopted standards.

lessons.title: Repair, alteration, rerating and pressure testing
lessons.body:
Distinguish restoring a component from changing its design basis. Replacing damaged material to an approved original configuration may be a repair, while a new nozzle, changed material, higher pressure or changed temperature can require alteration or rerating review. Classification depends on the governing rules, jurisdiction and actual scope, not the contractor's invoice label. Establish the authorized inspector, engineer and repair organization responsibilities before work.

A pressure test checks defined pressure-boundary behavior under specified conditions. It does not independently prove resistance to every future mechanism, and it does not replace required weld examination. The approved plan establishes test pressure, metal temperature, medium, boundaries, temporary connections, calibrated instrumentation, overpressure protection, exclusion and restoration. Pneumatic testing generally introduces substantially more stored energy than a comparable liquid-filled test and needs its own justified safeguards.

Static head matters. With water density taken as 1000 kg/m³, elevation difference 10 m and g = 9.81 m/s², pressure at the lower point is approximately 98.1 kPa greater than at the upper point. A gauge at the top therefore does not show the pressure at the bottom. This arithmetic does not select a test pressure.

Workshop task: review a proposed nozzle alteration with only a leak-test certificate. Produce the missing design, qualification, examination and test/restoration evidence list. The assessor checks that the learner identifies the changed design boundary and hydrostatic head, and does not prescribe an unsupported production test. Final release requires actual results and authorized disposition, not merely an approved plan.

lessons.title: Code navigation and integrated vessel disposition
lessons.body:
An inspector must identify the applicable document before finding a favorable paragraph. Separate the original construction code, in-service inspection code, jurisdictional requirements, owner specifications and any fitness-for-service methodology. Record edition/addenda and the exact equipment scope. For examination preparation, the API publication effectivity sheet identifies the examination-window references; a newer publication is not automatically the exam reference.

Use a repeatable navigation sequence: classify the component and decision; find scope and definitions; locate the applicable calculation or inspection rule; review exceptions and cross-references; record inputs and conclusion. A table entry without its notes can be wrong. An inspection interval provision cannot be used to waive an immediate unacceptable condition.

Capstone: a vessel has 10.8 mm measured wall, engineering-established required thickness 8.4 mm, recent corrosion rate 0.30 mm/year, an unexamined support and a proposed pressure increase. The eight-year arithmetic remaining life addresses only the supplied thinning model. It neither disposes of the unexamined support nor approves the pressure increase. The correct package separates current-condition evaluation, supplementary inspection and rerating analysis.

Assessment requires a marked vessel drawing, thickness/rate worksheet, source register, uncertainty log and signed recommendation distinguishing acceptable evidence from open decisions. Score identity/traceability, mechanism selection, calculations, governing-rule navigation and disposition separately. Each must be satisfactory; incorrect units, invented joint efficiency or approving an unresolved pressure boundary is a critical failure requiring remediation and reassessment. Passing this original VNDRLY assessment documents the taught knowledge and casework; API eligibility, examination and authorized field practice remain separate.

questions.prompt: A separator has water pooling at its bottom. Which plan best addresses the mechanism?

options.label: Target the lower shell and liquid interfaces with methods suitable for localized loss.
Use normal pressure as wall-thickness evidence.
Treat the whole vessel as one uniform reading.

questions.prompt: Which input is necessary before using a material allowable stress?

options.label: Verified material and applicable temperature/code basis.

questions.prompt: An insulated support region cannot be examined. How should it appear in the report?

options.label: An explicit coverage limitation with a disposition requirement.

questions.prompt: 12.0 mm falls to 10.8 mm in six years. What is the long-term rate?
At 10.8 mm current thickness, 8.4 mm required and 0.30 mm/year, calculated remaining life is:
A 0.1 mm apparent loss is smaller than measurement uncertainty. What follows?

options.label: Assign exactly 0.1 mm/year regardless of elapsed time.
Declare the instrument unusable in all applications.
Confirm comparability and uncertainty before assigning a precise rate.

questions.prompt: Using PD/(2t), P=1 MPa, D=1000 mm and t=10 mm gives:
In the supplied t=PR/(SE−0.6P) model, lowering E while holding other inputs constant does what?
Why cannot the thin-wall hoop equation establish the whole vessel rating?

options.label: It excludes other component rules, loads and applicability limits.
Pressure has no relation to stress.
Only the name of the inspector establishes rating.

questions.prompt: Which record establishes the person’s qualified welding range?
Which method requires ferromagnetic material?
An NDE report names weld 14 while the repaired weld is 41. What is required?

options.label: Apply the result to every weld on the vessel.
Traceable reconciliation before using the result for weld 41.
Assume the numbers were transposed and sign.

questions.prompt: A new nozzle changes the pressure boundary. What must happen first?

options.label: Classify and engineer the change under the applicable alteration requirements.
Call it maintenance to avoid review.
Use the last leak test as approval.

questions.prompt: With water, a point 10 m lower has approximately how much greater static pressure?
What does an approved test plan prove?

options.label: Every weld is free of flaws.
The planned method has been reviewed, not that the test passed.

questions.prompt: Which edition should an API candidate use for an examination window?

options.label: The oldest edition used by their employer.
The editions identified in that window’s effectivity sheet.
Any edition with the same cover color.

questions.prompt: Does eight years of calculated thinning life approve a pressure increase?

options.label: No; rerating and other unresolved conditions require separate evaluation.
Yes, if the exterior paint is intact.
Yes, if the operator signs a training attendance sheet.

questions.prompt: A favorable table value conflicts with a limiting table note. What controls the analysis?

options.label: Ignore notes because numbers are more precise.
Choose the less restrictive value automatically.
Average the note and the value.
Read and apply the note and governing scope with the table.

coverage: Six vessel-specific lessons: damage mapping, rate/life arithmetic, pressure/stress models, welding/NDE, alteration/testing and integrated disposition. Existing G70/G72/G77 supply supporting coordination concepts.
limitations: Not a complete API 510 examination preparation course: licensed construction/in-service code clauses, all head/nozzle/external-pressure calculations and an edition-by-edition objective crosswalk are not supplied. Numerical examples are explicitly limited educational models. Actual inspector eligibility, examination and field authorization remain external.

content.title: Asset Integrity | Piping Inspection | Applied Practice
content.description: Original VNDRLY instruction, worked cases and explained assessments. Complete the supporting courses in the certificate bundle as well. Practical competence and named external credentials follow the requirements stated in that bundle.

explanations.OG21_specialist_1_check1: Circuits support mechanism-based inspection; geometrical convenience alone is insufficient.
explanations.OG21_specialist_1_check2: Dead legs may retain corrosive phases despite low flow.
explanations.OG21_specialist_1_check3: Vibration-induced cyclic stress can damage a branch independently of main-line thinning.
explanations.OG21_specialist_2_check1: One millimetre divided by five years is 0.20 mm/year.
explanations.OG21_specialist_2_check2: The 2.1 mm margin divided by 0.30 mm/year gives seven years.
explanations.OG21_specialist_2_check3: Actual wall can vary due to manufacturing tolerance and service loss.
explanations.OG21_specialist_3_check1: The allowance is added to the calculated pressure thickness.
explanations.OG21_specialist_3_check2: Divide by 0.875 because the delivered minimum may be only 87.5 percent of nominal.
explanations.OG21_specialist_3_check3: Pressure-temperature ratings depend on the actual standard and material, not just the class number.
explanations.OG21_specialist_4_check1: Temporary repairs require controlled conditions and a defined continuing-management obligation.
explanations.OG21_specialist_4_check2: Material changes affect welding, thermal behavior, corrosion and ratings.
explanations.OG21_specialist_4_check3: Support condition affects loads, and records must reflect the actual installed configuration.
explanations.OG21_specialist_5_check2: Boundary traceability is necessary to apply a result to specific piping.
explanations.OG21_specialist_5_check3: Test success does not establish that normal protective functions have been restored.
explanations.OG21_specialist_6_check1: Different local mechanisms and missing coverage cannot be resolved by another location’s calculation.
explanations.OG21_specialist_6_check2: A number without its basis cannot be independently checked or applied to changed conditions.
explanations.OG21_specialist_6_check3: Honest incompleteness preserves the boundary; fabricated references create false acceptance.

lessons.title: Piping circuits and location-specific damage
lessons.body:
A piping inspection circuit groups components with sufficiently similar material, process environment and damage behavior to support a coherent plan. It is not merely everything carrying the same line number. Map pressure, temperature, phases, chemistry, flow regime, material changes and past failures. Circuit boundaries should change when these factors change enough to alter expected damage.

Injection points and mixing zones can experience concentrated chemistry or thermal gradients. Dead legs may collect water or deposits despite little flow. Soil-to-air interfaces, supports and damaged insulation create external-corrosion opportunities. Elbows, reducers and impingement locations may have erosion-corrosion. Small-bore branches can suffer vibration fatigue even when main-line thickness is satisfactory. These locations justify targeted examination rather than uniformly spaced convenience readings.

Consider a hot hydrocarbon line receiving a water-based additive. Downstream mixing can produce a local corrosive environment absent upstream. A branch normally isolated by a valve still contains stagnant fluid; marking it inactive does not remove it from the integrity system. Build a separate hypothesis for each region and identify the upstream/downstream extent requiring examination under the approved plan.

Workshop: mark an isometric with circuit boundaries, condition-monitoring locations, dead legs, injection zones, supports and access limitations. For every location, explain the mechanism and method selection. The assessor rejects a plan that averages a damaged elbow into a long straight-run thickness, omits a dead leg, or treats piping class as proof of actual material. The output is an inspection plan with explicit boundaries, not a field authorization.

lessons.title: Piping wall loss and remaining-life calculations
lessons.body:
Compare measurements at traceable locations using a consistent technique. Suppose a pipe location measured 7.8 mm five years ago and now measures 6.8 mm. Long-term loss is 1.0 mm, so the rate is 0.20 mm/year. If it measured 7.4 mm two years ago, the recent rate is 0.30 mm/year. The higher recent rate may reflect process acceleration, but first verify location and measurement comparability.

With an engineering-established required wall of 4.7 mm, the current margin is 2.1 mm. At 0.30 mm/year, the arithmetic remaining life is seven years. Do not label that result the inspection interval. Applicable classification, code maxima, mechanism uncertainty and approved RBI decisions may require earlier work. A local groove or crack cannot be accepted by averaging it with sound adjacent metal.

Nominal schedule thickness is a purchasing designation, not measured current thickness. Manufacturing tolerance and corrosion allowance are distinct concepts. When selecting replacement pipe, the code calculation must address required pressure thickness, allowances and applicable manufacturing tolerance. Do not subtract corrosion allowance twice or use a nominal wall as if it were a guaranteed minimum.

Exercise: prepare a three-date trend and a sensitivity case at 0.40 mm/year. The latter gives 2.1/0.40 = 5.25 years, showing how a plausible rate change affects planning. Record assumptions and identify what additional process history or examination would reduce uncertainty. An assessor verifies units, location identity and the distinction between a screening life calculation and an authorized continued-service decision.

lessons.title: Pressure thickness, components and flange ratings
lessons.body:
For arithmetic training, use the supplied straight-pipe model t = PD/[2(SEW+PY)]. With P = 2 MPa, outside diameter D = 200 mm, S = 100 MPa, E = 1, W = 1 and Y = 0.4, t = 400/[2(100+0.8)] = 1.984 mm. Add a supplied 1.5 mm allowance to obtain 3.484 mm. If a supplied negative manufacturing tolerance is 12.5%, a nominal selection must satisfy nominal ×0.875 ≥3.484; the resulting minimum nominal value is approximately 3.982 mm before selecting an available suitable product.

This is a deliberately supplied exercise, not an assertion that the equation or factors apply to every service. Actual applicability includes code edition, material, temperature, geometry and range limits. Bends, branch reinforcement, threaded regions, external loads, flexibility and special service may require additional checks. Pressure-only arithmetic does not assess all piping stresses.

A flange class is not a pressure value in psi. Allowable pressure depends on material group, temperature and the adopted rating table. A Class 150 marking cannot be interpreted as universally safe at 150 psi or any other fixed value. The assembly includes bolts, gasket, facing, valve and connections; incompatible components can defeat an otherwise adequate flange selection.

The assessment provides a fictional rating table and component list. The learner must choose the correct material/temperature row, identify the lowest applicable assembly limitation and preserve table notes. Incorrect diameter convention, omitted tolerance or assuming class equals pressure is a critical arithmetic or interpretation error.

lessons.title: Welding repairs and temporary interventions
lessons.body:
A repair plan begins with the defect mechanism and the affected boundary. Replacing a spool removes damaged material but introduces new welds, supports, alignment and testing requirements. A welded attachment or sleeve can redistribute stress or create an inaccessible corrosion region. A temporary repair is an engineered, time-bounded disposition, not permission to defer indefinitely.

Review WPS and welder scope, material traceability, fit-up, heat treatment, examination and pressure/leak-test requirements before installation. A change from one welding process to another may affect procedure and personnel qualifications. A repair on a line with environmental cracking cannot be justified solely by a thickness calculation. The repaired location and adjacent susceptible material need the mechanism addressed.

In a synthetic case, a carbon-steel spool is replaced with an alloy spool because it is available. Higher purchase cost does not establish compatibility. Thermal expansion, weldability, galvanic behavior, pressure-temperature properties and process chemistry require review. The correct action is a controlled material substitution decision, not unilateral installation.

Assessment uses an offline repair dossier with an expired temporary-repair date, missing filler traceability and incomplete NDE coverage. The learner lists each discrepancy, the technical consequence and the required owner/engineering disposition. The assessor requires a proposed completion plan that includes restoration of supports and insulation, updated isometric and next inspection requirements. No live leak sealing, welding on pressurized piping or unsupported clamp selection is taught or authorized by this case.

lessons.title: Testing, static head and reinstatement
lessons.body:
A piping test boundary must include every connected item actually exposed to test pressure. Show blinds, test manifolds, instruments, vents and excluded equipment on a controlled drawing. A closed valve symbol does not independently establish adequate isolation. The approved procedure addresses medium compatibility, temperature, pressure ramp, hold, acceptance, depressurization and emergency response.

Static head changes pressure with elevation. For water, a low point 20 m below a high-point gauge experiences about 196.2 kPa additional pressure. When a high point needs a specified minimum pressure, verify that low points and connected components remain within their permitted limits. The test engineer must resolve any conflict; inspectors should not simply move the gauge to obtain a favorable reading.

Record calibration identities, actual pressure/temperature/time history, leaks and repairs. Temperature changes can affect a closed-system pressure trace; a pressure decline requires evaluation, not automatic acceptance or automatic diagnosis of a leak. Pneumatic tests demand their distinct stored-energy controls. A test certificate with no boundary cannot prove which branch was tested.

Reinstatement is a separate verified stage. Remove temporary items through the approved process, restore relief devices and instruments, confirm valve positions and complete leak-tightness or functional checks required by the plan. In the practical desk exercise, an assessor plants an omitted branch and a relief device left isolated. Both must be identified. Evidence comprises the marked boundary, test record review and independently checked reinstatement list.

lessons.title: Piping capstone and code-based reporting
lessons.body:
The final report links each conclusion to equipment identity, condition, applicable criteria and authorized disposition. Separate observed data from inferred mechanism, calculated prediction and acceptance. Include isometric revision, circuit and monitoring-location identifiers, technique/coverage, current thickness, prior comparable values, calculated rates, required-thickness basis, limitations and the next action.

In the capstone, the main run has seven years of calculated thinning life, a branch has vibration indications, and an injection point has no recent coverage. The correct disposition is not a single green line-status icon. The main-run calculation is retained with its assumptions; branch fatigue and injection-zone uncertainty need their own examination and engineering decisions. A maximum code interval cannot waive a known unresolved condition.

Practice navigating an owner-supplied licensed reference: find the circuit classification, inspection requirements, repairs and rating provisions relevant to this exact case; record edition, paragraph and exception. If the reference is unavailable, identify the missing decision basis instead of fabricating a clause. API 570 examination references are tied to the examination window, so preparation should use the corresponding effectivity sheet.

An assessor evaluates a complete dossier for five outcomes: accurate circuit boundaries, correct arithmetic, mechanism-sensitive method selection, traceable rule application and defensible disposition. Every outcome must pass. Concealing missing coverage, approving unsupported rerating or replacing a reading with a nominal dimension is a critical failure. Retain first-attempt work, feedback and corrected independent work as distinct records.

questions.prompt: What is a sound basis for inspection-circuit boundaries?

options.label: Similar material, process conditions and expected damage mechanisms.
One paint color throughout the plant.

questions.prompt: Why inspect a normally isolated dead leg?

options.label: Its thickness equals the main run by definition.
Stagnant liquid or deposits can create localized corrosion.

questions.prompt: Main-line thickness is satisfactory but a small branch vibrates. Which concern remains?

options.label: No concern because the main line passed.
Fatigue cracking at the branch connection.
Only uniform corrosion in the main run.

questions.prompt: 7.8 mm becomes 6.8 mm in five years. Rate equals:
At 6.8 mm current, 4.7 mm required and 0.30 mm/year, remaining life is:
Can nominal schedule thickness replace a current UT reading?

options.label: Yes, if the pipe is painted.
Yes, if the schedule number is large.
No; it describes a nominal product dimension, not current condition.

questions.prompt: The supplied pressure-only calculation gives 1.984 mm and allowance is 1.5 mm. Total before tolerance is:
A required minimum is 3.484 mm and negative tolerance is 12.5%. Minimum nominal is about:
What does Class 150 mean for flange pressure selection?

options.label: Use the applicable material-temperature rating table and notes.
The flange always permits exactly 150 psi.

questions.prompt: What makes a temporary repair acceptable as a managed condition?

options.label: Calling it temporary on an invoice.
An approved engineered basis, defined limits and a tracked expiry or review date.

questions.prompt: A higher-cost alloy spool is available. Can it replace carbon steel without review?

options.label: Yes, every alloy has identical expansion.
No; compatibility and design implications must be assessed.

questions.prompt: Which repair completion item is easy to miss but technically relevant?

options.label: Only deleting the old defect record.
Restored supports and updated inspection records.

questions.prompt: A water-filled low point is 20 m below the gauge. Additional pressure is about:
A test certificate lacks the tested boundary. What is missing?

options.label: Evidence establishing which components the result covers.

questions.prompt: A successful test is complete, but a relief device remains isolated. Is operating release established?

options.label: Yes, if the test gauge is removed.
Yes, if the line number is correct.
No; reinstatement and protection must be verified.
Yes, pressure testing authorizes all valve positions.

questions.prompt: A main-run life calculation is favorable but an unexamined injection zone remains. What is correct?

options.label: Keep the calculation bounded and address the injection zone separately.
Apply the main-run life to every component.
Delete the injection location from the circuit.

questions.prompt: What should a required-thickness value in the report identify?

options.label: Its engineering/code basis and applicable inputs.

questions.prompt: When a governing clause is unavailable, the learner should:

options.label: Identify the unresolved decision and obtain the actual reference.

coverage: Six piping-specific lessons with circuit mapping, rate/life and pressure/tolerance calculations, flange interpretation, repair dossiers and test/reinstatement exercises.
limitations: Licensed API 570/574 and construction-code rules are not reproduced. Full examination-window BOK coverage, flexibility/branch calculations, actual owner classifications and practical inspector qualification remain unverified.

content.title: Asset Integrity | Storage Tank Inspection | Applied Practice
content.description: Original VNDRLY instruction, worked cases and explained assessments. Complete the supporting courses in the certificate bundle as well. Practical competence and named external credentials follow the requirements stated in that bundle.

explanations.OG22_specialist_1_check1: rho*g*h gives about 100062 Pa, which is 100 kPa.
explanations.OG22_specialist_1_check2: Liquid pressure is proportional to density at the same depth.
explanations.OG22_specialist_1_check3: The bottom and its underside require appropriate coverage beyond an exterior visual walkdown.
explanations.OG22_specialist_2_check1: Stress is inversely proportional to thickness, so 10/8 = 1.25.
explanations.OG22_specialist_2_check2: The 2 mm margin divided by 0.25 mm/year gives eight years.
explanations.OG22_specialist_2_check3: Both mechanical and chemical service assumptions can change.
explanations.OG22_specialist_3_check1: Coverage and method limitations bound the conclusion.
explanations.OG22_specialist_3_check2: Repeatable location is necessary for confirmation, repair and trending.
explanations.OG22_specialist_3_check3: Leak testing and wall-loss measurement are different inspection questions.
explanations.OG22_specialist_4_check2: A best-fit plane can conceal local distortion and associated stress.
explanations.OG22_specialist_4_check3: Brittle fracture depends on interacting material, loading and flaw conditions.
explanations.OG22_specialist_5_check1: Different tank components carry different loads and have different repair rules.
explanations.OG22_specialist_5_check2: Inspection must occur while the feature can actually be examined.
explanations.OG22_specialist_5_check3: Material identity does not establish weld soundness or complete required coverage.
explanations.OG22_specialist_6_check1: Density and chemical/environmental conditions can both change.
explanations.OG22_specialist_6_check2: Shell and bottom environments, mechanisms and coverage differ.
explanations.OG22_specialist_6_check3: Revision history supports traceable integrity management without misrepresenting old evidence as current.

lessons.title: Tank components, load paths and deterioration
lessons.body:
An aboveground storage tank transfers liquid load through its shell, bottom and foundation. Identify shell courses, horizontal and vertical seams, bottom and annular plates where present, roof structure, nozzles, reinforcement, anchorage and foundation. A floating roof introduces seals, drains, pontoons and travel clearances; a fixed roof introduces its own support and venting arrangements. Inspect the actual tank type rather than applying one generic checklist.

Hydrostatic pressure increases with liquid depth. For a liquid density of 850 kg/m³ and depth 12 m, bottom pressure is rho*g*h = 850*9.81*12 = 100062 Pa, about 100 kPa. The upper shell sees less liquid head than the lower shell. This explains why shell-course thickness and location matter. Changing stored product density or permitted fill height can change loading even without a pressure-vessel-style operating pressure increase.

Separate product-side corrosion from soil-side bottom corrosion. Water bottoms, deposits and microbial activity may create localized attack; drainage and foundation conditions influence underside damage. Roof drain failure can add load to a floating roof. Blocked venting can create pressure or vacuum conditions the tank was not designed to sustain.

Exercise: mark the load path and damage locations on a tank sketch. The assessor requires a distinct rationale for shell, bottom, roof and foundation examinations. Missing underside coverage must remain visible. A routine exterior walkdown cannot establish bottom integrity or justify a higher fill level.

lessons.title: Shell evaluation and fill-height reasoning
lessons.body:
Shell evaluation connects measured condition to an approved required-thickness basis for each course and loading condition. Do not combine readings from different elevations into one average and assume the result represents the most highly loaded region. Local thin areas, pits and weld conditions require their applicable evaluation rules rather than arbitrary averaging.

For teaching only, a thin-cylinder liquid-head model gives hoop stress sigma = rho*g*h*D/(2t). With rho = 1000 kg/m³, h = 10 m, D = 20 m and t = 0.010 m, sigma is 98.1 MPa. If thickness falls to 0.008 m, this model gives 122.6 MPa. All lengths must be converted consistently. This model omits actual tank-code factors, course-specific formulas, joints and local conditions and cannot establish a field fill limit.

If engineering has independently established required thickness 7.0 mm, measured thickness is 9.0 mm and a defensible uniform rate is 0.25 mm/year, arithmetic life is eight years. The rate and required thickness must correspond to the same location and service. A planned switch to a heavier product invalidates assumptions that depend on density.

Assessment: calculate the two model stresses and remaining life, then list why neither alone establishes an allowable operating level. The assessor checks course identity, units, density assumptions and treatment of local damage. The accepted deliverable is a bounded worksheet and a request for the actual code evaluation, never an improvised tank rerating.

lessons.title: Bottom inspection, mapping and leak prevention
lessons.body:
Tank-bottom inspection needs a coordinate system that survives future outages. Map plate identifiers, welds, sumps, columns, repairs and reference directions. Describe inspected area and exclusions around obstructions. Magnetic-flux-leakage scanning can screen suitable ferromagnetic bottoms for metal loss, but sizing, near-weld zones, surface condition and tool capabilities must be addressed. Confirmatory UT provides local thickness evidence under the approved technique; it does not retroactively fill every unscanned area.

Distinguish general thinning, isolated pits and connected localized corrosion. A plate average can conceal a deep pit. Determine whether reported metal loss is product-side or underside where the method supports that distinction, and state ambiguity otherwise. Vacuum-box examination of suitable welds addresses leakage paths under the specified procedure, not the entire remaining wall of the bottom.

In a synthetic outage, 90% of the floor is screened and several column areas are inaccessible. The report must state actual coverage, confirm sizing of relevant indications and assign the excluded areas a technical disposition. An owner cannot infer 100% bottom acceptance by multiplying the inspected area by a favorable average thickness.

Practical assessment uses a clean training plate or data set containing mapped artificial loss and a weld leak indication. A qualified assessor checks instrument setup under the supplied procedure, accurate coordinates, correct confirmation decisions and bounded reporting. Fabricating readings or changing the coverage percentage is a critical failure. Actual entry and work conditions require their own permits and controls.

lessons.title: Settlement, distortion and brittle-fracture screening
lessons.body:
Settlement is not a single number. Uniform settlement lowers the whole tank; planar tilt rotates its overall plane; differential settlement distorts the shell or bottom; localized edge settlement creates concentrated deformation near the shell-bottom region. These shapes have different effects on stresses, drains, roof travel, piping connections and seals. Use stable survey references and a consistent coordinate convention.

Suppose opposing shell points 20 m apart differ in elevation by 40 mm. The simple slope is 0.040/20 = 0.002, or 0.2%. This describes tilt, not acceptability. A third point departing sharply from the best-fit plane may reveal differential distortion that the two-point slope conceals. Compare complete profiles under the actual tank standard and engineering method.

Brittle fracture involves material toughness, temperature, thickness, stress and flaws. An older tank with incomplete material records requires more than a warm-weather visual inspection before cold-service changes or major repairs. Hydrostatic testing can be an important event in the evaluation, but arbitrary cold testing is not a remedy. The engineering basis must address material and temperature restrictions.

Assessment provides eight survey points, a localized outlier and a proposed cold-service change. The learner distinguishes tilt from local distortion, computes the simple slope and identifies missing toughness/material evidence. The assessor rejects any claim that a small average slope proves every local condition acceptable or that an undocumented material can be assigned a convenient toughness value.

lessons.title: Tank repairs, welding and reconstruction controls
lessons.body:
A tank repair plan identifies the damaged component and the requirements for its restored condition. Bottom patches, shell inserts, nozzle changes and roof repairs have different geometry, weld and examination issues. Reconstruction adds identification and reassembly controls for reused material. Do not assume a method acceptable for a roof plate also suits a shell course or annular region.

Before work, confirm material identity, approved drawings, WPS/PQR basis, welder scope, joint preparation, dimensional tolerances, weld sequence and examination requirements. Repair geometry can create stress concentrations or interfere with drainage and future inspection. The technical authority must evaluate the actual design rather than accept a patch merely because it covers the visible damage.

Inspection hold points should occur while features remain accessible: material receipt, fit-up, root/back-gouge stages when applicable, completed weld examination and final dimensional checks. Leak testing, NDE and hydrostatic-test requirements come from the adopted standard and authorized engineering decision. A waiver requires its actual documented basis, not a scheduling preference.

In the assessment dossier, an insert plate has traceability but the welder record covers a different process, and final NDE omits a seam intersection. The learner must keep these as separate unresolved conditions. The assessor requires marked drawings, qualification comparison and a completed/held inspection-point register. A repair cannot be released merely because every purchased material certificate is present; workmanship and examination evidence must also be complete.

lessons.title: Tank inspection plan and capstone dossier
lessons.body:
An integrated tank plan separates routine in-service observations, external inspections, thickness work and internal outage examinations. The applicable intervals depend on the adopted code, service, corrosion basis, bottom safeguards, inspection history and any qualified risk-based methodology. Do not manufacture a universal interval from one thickness calculation.

Capstone: a tank changes from a lighter product to water service, has an eight-year arithmetic shell life under the old assumptions, incomplete bottom coverage and a settlement outlier. The learner must revisit liquid-head loading, changed corrosion environment, bottom uncertainty and settlement independently. A favorable shell trend cannot dispose of the bottom or foundation.

The final dossier contains a component register, drawings, thickness and settlement maps, calculations with assumptions, repair/NDE records, applicable reference editions, limitations and proposed actions. For each conclusion, state whether it is measured, calculated, inferred or accepted by the responsible authority. Preserve superseded conclusions with their revision history so future inspectors understand why the operating envelope changed.

Assessment criteria are component/load understanding, correct calculations, inspection-method coverage, settlement reasoning and traceable disposition. All five must be satisfactory. Unsupported fill-height approval, invented bottom readings or ignored local settlement is a critical failure. The course supplies original knowledge and casework; it does not supply every licensed API 653/API 650 calculation, a complete examination crosswalk or an API credential. Actual tanks require qualified inspectors and engineering decisions using their records and governing requirements.

lessons.title: Inspection authority and construction quality planning
lessons.body:
A pipeline construction inspector verifies work against approved requirements and records deviations. The inspector does not redesign the line from personal preference or silently change acceptance criteria. Establish the contract hierarchy, approved drawings, specifications, permits, applicable regulatory scope and the inspector's delegated hold/release authority. Distinguish observation, witness point, hold point and nonconformance disposition in the project plan.

An inspection and test plan places checks before irreversible concealment. Typical stages include material receipt, right-of-way controls, excavation, bending, welding, NDE, coating, lowering-in, backfill, testing and restoration. Each checkpoint needs a criterion, responsible party, required evidence and release authority. A hold point cannot be cleared by attendance alone.

Daily reports should identify location by station/chainage and coordinates where required, date/time, weather, crew, work performed, inspected quantity, findings and outstanding issues. Separate direct observations from contractor statements. A photograph needs location, orientation and scale when used for dimensional evidence. Preserve original records and corrections rather than backdating a clean report.

In an exercise, a contractor wants to backfill a coated joint before holiday-test results arrive. The learner identifies the applicable hold point, records the affected location and prevents concealment through the authorized process. The assessor requires an inspection record, a nonconformance description and a release decision tied to evidence. The goal is traceable quality control without inventing authority the inspector has not been delegated.

lessons.title: Right-of-way, excavation and environmental interfaces
lessons.body:
Construction inspection must connect the installed route with land, utility and environmental restrictions. Verify survey control, approved alignment, limits of disturbance, crossing permits, erosion controls and sensitive-area boundaries before ground disturbance. A proposed route drawing is not proof that underground utilities have been located or safely exposed. Utility information, locating marks and the excavation plan must be reconciled with actual field conditions.

Excavation hazards change with soil, depth, water, vibration, adjacent loads and weather. The employer's competent person evaluates the excavation and required protective system. Inspectors observe whether required controls and access are in place but should not invent a soil classification from a distant photograph. Stop and escalate conflicting utility indications, unexpected structures, water ingress or changing ground conditions through project authority.

Environmental measures must follow the site permits and plan. Separate topsoil where required, maintain sediment controls and protect water crossings. A route deviation around an obstruction can change cover, bending, property and permit assumptions; it requires controlled approval and as-built survey.

Case: the crew moves 3 m outside the approved corridor to avoid rock. The learner identifies alignment, permit, landowner and design implications, records station limits and requests the authorized change process. Practical assessment requires a marked route plan and a field walk with a qualified assessor. Critical failures include approving an unlocated utility crossing, entering an unprotected excavation or calling a proposed deviation an as-built record.

lessons.title: Pipe receipt, bending and weld traceability
lessons.body:
Material control starts before pipe enters the trench. Reconcile purchase specifications, markings, heat numbers, material certificates, dimensions and condition. Damaged bevels, dents, gouges or coating require the applicable evaluation; do not grind or repair a pressure-boundary defect without an approved method. Preserve identity when pieces are cut so installed segments remain traceable.

Cold bends change geometry and can introduce ovality, wrinkling or coating damage. Verify the approved bending procedure, equipment, location and dimensional acceptance basis. A bend that fits the trench is not automatically acceptable. Pipe grade, wall, seam position and bend geometry may matter under the actual specification.

Weld maps connect joint number, pipe identities, WPS, welder IDs, date and NDE. Before welding, verify fit-up, cleanliness, approved procedure revision and personnel range. During production, record required parameters and controls. After welding, retain repairs and reexamination in the same traceable chain rather than replacing a failed result with a clean final page.

Assessment: a 12 m pipe is cut into two pieces, but only one retains its heat mark; a weld map lists a welder not on the approved roster. The learner must reconcile both before acceptance. The assessor checks actual identity transfer, map consistency and a comparison against supplied fictional WPS limits. Changing a heat number from memory or treating a radiograph as proof of material grade is a critical failure.

lessons.title: Coating, lowering-in and backfill
lessons.body:
Pipeline coating is a barrier system whose performance depends on surface preparation, application, cure, continuity and damage control. Confirm the coating procedure and product requirements for surface condition, ambient conditions, mixing where applicable, thickness and cure. A visually uniform coating can contain holidays or inadequate adhesion. Holiday testing must use the correct method and voltage for the specified coating and thickness; arbitrary high voltage can damage the coating.

Before lowering-in, inspect coating condition, repairs, trench bedding and lifting arrangements. Controlled supports prevent excessive bending or concentrated damage. The lifting plan and equipment capacities belong to competent lifting personnel; the inspector verifies the specified checks and records deviations. Dragging the line across abrasive ground can invalidate previously satisfactory coating evidence.

Backfill can damage coating or create concentrated loads if unsuitable material or placement is used. Verify padding, cover, separation and warning/marker requirements against the actual design and permits. Survey installed position before concealment. Future maintenance needs actual location, depth and crossing information rather than the proposed route.

A practical exercise uses a training coated pipe with deliberately introduced safe defects and a supplied procedure. The learner documents surface condition, verifies instrument setup with the assessor, maps indications, records approved repairs and rechecks repaired locations. Acceptance requires traceable results and correct limits; a generic statement that the line was checked is insufficient. Actual energized holiday testing requires trained personnel and the approved equipment procedure.

lessons.title: Pressure-test review and numerical checks
lessons.body:
The inspector reviews a pressure-test package against the approved project basis. Identify segment boundaries, elevations, material and component limitations, test medium, temperature, pressure limits, hold period, instrumentation, disposal and exclusion controls. Pressure testing is a controlled high-energy activity; this course does not authorize selecting test pressures or standing near a pressurized boundary.

Use static-head arithmetic to understand the plan. A water-filled test segment with 30 m elevation difference has about 294.3 kPa pressure difference between high and low points. If a supplied fictional high-point target is 5.0 MPa, the low point is approximately 5.294 MPa, ignoring other effects. Every component must be evaluated for its actual pressure; one gauge value cannot be applied uniformly over elevation.

Volume calculations help reconcile planned fill quantities. A simplified 1 km segment with 0.30 m internal diameter has volume pi*D²*L/4 = approximately 70.7 m³. Real fill volumes include fittings and boundaries, and trapped air must be controlled under the approved procedure. An unexpected volume discrepancy warrants review, not concealment.

Assessment requires independently checking the elevation correction and volume, reviewing gauge calibration and tracing the recorded hold period. The learner must identify temperature effects and missing boundary evidence without inventing a leak diagnosis. Pass only when the report distinguishes planned values, measured values and authorized interpretation.

lessons.title: Restoration, turnover and practical inspection assessment
lessons.body:
Closeout verifies both the constructed asset and the obligations surrounding it. Reconcile as-built surveys, material and weld maps, NDE, coating repairs, test records, cathodic-protection interfaces where applicable, crossing records, valve identification and outstanding nonconformances. Restoration includes erosion controls, drainage, topsoil, land commitments and monitoring required by permits. A mechanically complete line may still have unresolved environmental obligations.

Create a punch list with location, requirement, finding, owner, due date and closure evidence. Distinguish a cosmetic item from a pressure-boundary, location or protective-system issue. The project authority decides commissioning readiness under its requirements; the inspector should not bury critical incomplete work in a general accepted-with-comments label.

Capstone: a completed segment has a passing pressure test, two unresolved coating repairs, one missing heat transfer and a route deviation absent from the survey. The passing test does not resolve any of those identity, corrosion-protection or location deficiencies. The learner prepares a bounded turnover recommendation and identifies each needed closure.

The practical rubric requires an assessor-observed review of a mock construction spread and dossier. Evaluate traceability, dimensional checks using supplied criteria, correct hold-point action, clear reporting and escalation. Each must pass; falsified witness status, concealed nonconformance or unsafe entry is a critical failure. API 1169 eligibility and examination remain separate, and actual project specifications/regulatory scope must be supplied for job acceptance.

lessons.title: Welding processes and inspection consequences
lessons.body:
Shielded metal arc welding uses a consumable flux-covered electrode; the coating contributes shielding and slag. Gas metal arc welding uses a continuously fed wire and external shielding gas. Flux-cored arc welding uses tubular wire, with shielding supplied by flux and sometimes external gas. Gas tungsten arc welding uses a nonconsumable tungsten electrode and separate filler when needed. Submerged arc welding operates under granular flux. These differences affect access, productivity, discontinuities and the variables an inspector must verify.

Shielding protects the molten weld pool from atmospheric contamination. Wind or unsuitable gas flow can compromise gas-shielded processes. Slag-producing processes require appropriate cleaning between passes; trapped slag is not eliminated by a smooth final cap. GTAW tungsten contamination and GMAW lack of fusion are different concerns requiring different evidence. Do not assign a process merely from bead appearance when records are available.

Current, voltage and travel speed influence energy input and bead shape, but procedure limits govern production. Increasing travel speed at unchanged electrical power reduces energy per unit length. A broad bead is not proof of complete fusion at the root or sidewall. Joint access and technique also affect the result.

Assessment: identify processes from equipment diagrams, explain the shielding mechanism and match likely discontinuities to inspection opportunities. The assessor supplies a WPS and asks which observable variables must be recorded. Pass requires correct process identification and a rationale; memorizing an acronym without recognizing its inspection consequences is insufficient.

lessons.title: Metallurgy, heat input and discontinuity reasoning
lessons.body:
A fusion weld includes deposited weld metal, a heat-affected zone and unaffected base metal. Cooling history, composition and restraint influence hardness, toughness, distortion and residual stress. In susceptible steels, hydrogen, a hard microstructure and tensile stress can combine to produce delayed cracking. Controls may include consumable handling, approved preheat/interpass practice and qualified heat treatment; an inspector verifies the specified controls rather than inventing temperatures.

For an educational electrical-energy calculation, heat input before efficiency correction is voltage × current ×60 divided by travel speed in mm/min, producing joules/mm. At 24 V, 200 A and 240 mm/min, the value is 1200 J/mm or 1.2 kJ/mm. A supplied efficiency factor of 0.8 would give 0.96 kJ/mm in that model. Actual code definitions and procedure limits must be checked before using an efficiency factor.

Distinguish porosity, slag inclusion, undercut, overlap, lack of fusion, incomplete penetration and cracking. A discontinuity becomes a defect when it fails applicable acceptance criteria. Shape, orientation, location and service matter; the same length limit cannot be assumed for every indication. Cracks require particularly careful evaluation under the governing standard.

Practical desk assessment uses section sketches and photographs with known answers. Learners identify plausible discontinuities, state what the image cannot prove and choose further examination. The assessor checks the heat-input arithmetic and rejects acceptance based on appearance alone or an invented universal discontinuity limit.

lessons.title: Drawings, welding symbols and dimensional interpretation
lessons.body:
A welding symbol communicates the joint requirement through a reference line, arrow and applicable symbols, dimensions and notes. Use the drawing's adopted symbol standard; arrow-side conventions and supplementary information must be interpreted under that standard. Do not infer a weld on both sides from a single-side requirement or omit a tail note identifying a process or specification.

Joint geometry includes groove angle, root opening, root face, alignment and backing where specified. Fillet weld leg size and effective throat are different dimensions. For an ideal equal-leg fillet with a 90-degree joint, the geometric throat is approximately 0.707 times the leg. A 6 mm leg therefore gives about 4.24 mm geometric throat. Actual effective throat rules can differ with penetration and code provisions; this geometry exercise is not a universal design rule.

Intermittent weld length and pitch describe different things. In a fictional drawing requiring 50 mm weld segments on 150 mm center-to-center pitch, the clear nominal gap is 100 mm along a simple straight arrangement. A note requiring continuous sealing would conflict with interpreting the joint as intermittently sealed; resolve drawing conflicts before fabrication.

Assessment uses a controlled drawing with three welds and a dimensional specimen. The learner translates each symbol into a plain-language requirement and marks the measurement locations. The assessor verifies side, length, size and notes. Critical failures include fabricating a missing dimension or measuring reinforcement as if it were the specified fillet leg.

lessons.title: WPS, PQR and performance qualification
lessons.body:
The WPS states how production welding is to be performed. A PQR records actual qualification variables and test outcomes supporting the procedure where required. A welder performance qualification records an individual's demonstrated range. Prequalified procedures exist under some standards and conditions, but prequalification is not a universal exemption from controlled instructions or personnel qualification.

Build a comparison matrix: production process, material grouping, thickness, diameter where relevant, position, joint/backing, filler, shielding, electrical characteristics, preheat/interpass and heat treatment. Compare each to the WPS and governing qualification rules. Essential, supplementary essential and nonessential variable categories are code-specific; a familiar term does not justify applying one code's ranges to another.

Case: production requires GTAW root plus SMAW fill. The welder record covers only SMAW. The WPS may be valid for both processes, but this person's GTAW scope is not established. A second case has a valid welder record but an unapproved shielding-gas substitution; personnel qualification does not approve the procedure change.

Assessment requires two complete matrices and supporting references from supplied licensed documents. The assessor checks that the learner separates procedure and person, identifies every mismatch and avoids inventing qualified thickness ranges. A passing record names the actual document revision, qualification basis and unresolved items. Production release remains with the assigned authority.

lessons.title: Visual examination and measurement reliability
lessons.body:
Visual inspection occurs before, during and after welding. Before welding, check identification, fit-up, cleanliness, bevels and approved procedure/personnel scope. During welding, observe required parameters, preheat/interpass controls and cleaning. After welding, examine dimensions, profile and accessible discontinuities under suitable lighting and access. Final inspection cannot recover every hidden fit-up condition.

Select the correct gauge for the feature. A fillet gauge, bridge cam gauge, straightedge and ruler do not measure identical things. Verify instrument condition and zero/reference checks as applicable. Record units and measurement location. Surface roughness, access angle and inconsistent contact can create reading errors. Do not round a marginal value until the actual acceptance method permits it.

In a supplied fictional criterion, undercut must not exceed 0.5 mm. A measurement of 0.6 mm is nonconforming under that criterion; the inspector cannot round it to zero. If measurement uncertainty is significant near the limit, apply the specified decision rule or obtain a more suitable measurement. The fictional limit is not a general AWS acceptance value.

Practical assessment uses calibrated training replicas with known discontinuities and dimensional values. Require the learner to select the gauge, demonstrate contact, record repeated readings and apply supplied criteria. The assessor scores detection, measurement and disposition separately. Missing a planted crack-like indication or falsifying a reading is a critical failure; an uncertain measurement should be reported and resolved rather than hidden.

lessons.title: Code application and inspector practical capstone
lessons.body:
Inspection conclusions need the applicable construction/service code, edition, drawing revision and project criteria. A method standard may explain how to examine without specifying acceptance for the component. Find the correct acceptance section and its notes, joint type, loading category and examination extent. Do not transfer a pressure-piping limit to a structural weld because both are steel.

Capstone includes a drawing, WPS, PQR, welder records, heat certificates, parameter log, visual measurements and NDE report. The specimen has correct fillet dimensions but an undocumented procedure change and incomplete required NDE. Dimensional conformity alone does not close those gaps. The learner writes a report separating conforming measurements, nonconformances and unverified requirements.

Assessor rubric: identify all planted document conflicts; measure three features within the training specimen's established tolerance; correctly classify supplied discontinuities; cite the supplied acceptance basis; issue a bounded disposition. All domains must pass. Unsafe handling, invented readings or accepting a known unresolved critical condition requires remediation and a new independent attempt. Retain specimen identity and assessor qualifications with the evidence.

AWS CWI has its own eligibility, vision and examination requirements, including fundamentals, practical and code application. This original VNDRLY course develops specific knowledge and practical-review skills but does not claim complete CWI exam coverage, access to proprietary replicas or an AWS credential. Selected-code study with current authorized references remains necessary.
